pr_body:
This commits introduces check for standard interface and endpoint
requests. Not all requests shall be accepted. In particular those
which addresses not existing interfaces/endpoints should be STALLed.
This patch STALLes incorrect requests.

Signed-off-by: Emil Obalski <emil.obalski@nordicsemi.no>

Fixes: #27964
pr_comments: @jfischer-phytec-iot I've addressed Your comments + I've reworked `is_ep_valid()` + added checks for all `*_std_endpoint_req` following by the 2.0 spec. Please keep that in mind when revisiting.

issue_context.title: usb: Standard requests are not filtered.
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Standard USB Requests shall not always be accepted by the device.
Refering to the USB 2.0 specification standard USB are divided into 3 depending on the recipient:
- device (always accepted)
- interface (accepted only if the device is in **Configured** state and the requested interface is valid - existing)
- endpoint (for control endpoints (0x81, 0x00) accepted in **Addressed** state, for other accepted only if the device is in **Configured** state and the requested endpoint is valid - existing)

**Logs and console output**
* Endpoint request for Endpoint 1 is accepted in **Addressed** state.
![ep](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52450830/91967393-73bab980-ed13-11ea-9493-debe9408c6a0.PNG)
* Interface request for Interface 1 is accepted in **Addressed** state.
![if](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52450830/91967392-73222300-ed13-11ea-9e27-ddd5b8e6eb19.PNG)
* Interface request for not existing Interface 55 is accepted.
![if2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52450830/91967388-72898c80-ed13-11ea-8d75-5692c7868a2c.PNG)


**Expected behavior**
The device should accept only valid requests.

**Impact**
Possible data corruption.

review_comments: That can be simplified, just check `setup->wIndex`(L853) against bNumInterfaces from [Configuration Descriptor](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/usb/usb_descriptor.c#L92)
That's good point. I will test it.
